Flagship note

Blue Dart Express: Market-Perform, fair value Rs 4,326

Fairly priced at the market's own discount rate. Not a bargain, and not a short. Four findings carry the note.

Finding 1 · Cash

Cash after leases is a quarter of what a screen shows

Under Ind AS 116, rent on leased aircraft, hubs and vehicles leaves through financing cash flow, below the free cash flow line on most screens. Treated as the operating cost it is, FY26 free cash flow was Rs 131 crore, not Rs 496 crore.

Why it matters: the business is valued on cash after lease payments, not on EBITDA.

Finding 2 · Discount rate

The market is priced at a 2.40% equity premium, not 6%

From NSE's published ratios the Nifty 500 trades at 22.18x earnings. A textbook 6% premium values it at 10.0x, 55% below where it trades, so that rate cannot support a relative rating on one stock. The premium that reproduces the index is 2.40%, which gives Blue Dart a WACC of 9.19%.

Why it matters: a rating is a relative call, so the stock is discounted at the rate the market itself is priced at. At a 12% required return the value is Rs 2,455, and the note says so.

Finding 3 · What the price assumes

The price asks for what the company nearly delivers

Holding my cash flows, Rs 4,446 is reached at a WACC of 9.11%, almost exactly the market's rate. Holding my WACC, the price needs a 16.7% operating margin; the first half of FY27 delivered 15.9%. Half a point on the WACC moves fair value by about 15%.

Why it matters: the value is sensitive to one input, which is itself a reason not to take a strong view.

Market-Perform

Test the weakest input: beta

Daily returns over two years give a beta of 0.82 (NSE data), which supports the 0.8 in the note. Weekly returns give 1.06 (Bloomberg, two years against the Nifty 500, adjusted). On 1.06 the fair value is Rs 3,683 and the rating would be Underperform by 2 points. That is why I call this a low-conviction Market-Perform.

Interpolated between the points of the note's sensitivity table (terminal growth 6%). Rule: beyond 15% either way changes the rating.

4

Finding 4 · The rating

Market-Perform, with the triggers published

Fair value is 3% below the price, inside the 15% band set in advance. Not a bargain: FY27E EPS only gets back to FY22's level and receivable days have risen from 46 to 58. Not a short either: first-half profit is up 48%.

Why it matters: anyone can see in advance what would change the rating.

Quantitative research

Testing a strategy before trusting it

A backtest that showed a winning-looking strategy was a losing one.

QUANTITATIVE RESEARCH · Nifty options · Python

A 72.4% win rate that still lost money

  • 38.9M one-minute Nifty option bars from June 2021 to May 2026, 99.6% of every possible bar, with real traded prices for expired contracts at a 98% fill rate.
  • Black-Scholes repricing on every bar, with no look-ahead bias.
  • 77 Friday entries lost 770.5 points; every other weekday made money, 528.8 points in all. The put leg lost 295.8 points while the call leg made 54.1.
  • The worst single trade lost 457.7 points, almost twice the whole net loss.
  • 1,600+ trades tested in all: these 395 plus 1,234 opening-range trades on five years of data.

Source: author's backtest; trade log of 395 trades entered 1 Oct 2024 to 19 May 2026. Project initiated at Group Bayport.
